title: unsafe code, pointers, and fixed (interop box)
hook: unsafe lets you use pointers like C++ for tight interop with native libraries. fixed pins a managed object so the garbage collector cannot move it while native code holds the address. Keep unsafe in a small, reviewed box — most app code never needs it.

blocks.text: Enable unsafe in the project file for pointer syntax. Pointers point to raw memory — no bounds checks, no garbage collection tracking. fixed pins arrays or strings during a block so compaction does not move them. SkiaSharp and imaging libraries may use native pointers internally; you usually call safe wrappers instead of writing unsafe yourself.

entries.plainDefinition: C# context where pointer types and arithmetic are allowed.
Pins a managed object so the GC cannot relocate it during the block.
Preventing the collector from moving an object during compaction.

blocks.text: Excessive pinning fragments the heap — module 14 mark-compact cannot move pinned objects. Prefer Span and Memory when BCL APIs suffice. unsafe belongs in interop shims, not business logic. Code review should flag new unsafe blocks like C++ in a C# shop.

blocks.title: Prefer safe abstractions
blocks.body: Try Span, MemoryMarshal, and LibraryImport before hand-written pointers.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Enable AllowUnsafeBlocks
items.body: Only in projects that need interop.

items.title: Isolate in static class
items.body: One NativeMethods or Interop file, heavily reviewed.

items.title: Pin minimally
items.body: Short fixed blocks; free handles in finally.

items.title: Document lifetime
items.body: Native code must not use pointer after unpin.

diagram.title: fixed pinning scope
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Enter fixed block] --> B[Object pinned\nGC cannot move]
  B --> C[Pass pointer to native]
  C --> D[Exit fixed block]
  D --> E[Object unpinned\nGC can compact again]

snippet.label: Enable unsafe
snippet.explanation: Required for pointer syntax. Keep scoped to interop projects when possible.

snippet.label: fixed with byte array
snippet.explanation: fixed pins data for the block duration. After the block, GC can move the array again.

snippet.label: Span alternative without unsafe
snippet.explanation: Prefer Span APIs when native library offers them — SkiaSharp and modern BCL increasingly do.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Long-lived pinned handles — heap fragmentation. Returning pointer from method after fixed ends — use-after-free. Spreading unsafe through business layers instead of one interop shim.

interviewTakeaways: unsafe enables pointers; fixed pins objects during native calls.
Pinning prevents compaction — keep fixed blocks short.
Prefer Span and LibraryImport over hand-written unsafe when possible.
commonPitfalls: Pointer used after fixed block ends.
Pinning large arrays for entire request lifetime.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node N-API uses C++ pointers. C# unsafe is the in-language way to do similar pinning before calling native code.
